card.name: Gaga
card.era: 20th c. in DR (derived from Haitian Rara via sugar-labor migration)
card.tagline: Afro-Dominican Holy Week procession, the local form of Haitian Rara.
card.profile: Gaga (Haitian Rara, creolized to gaga in the DR) is an Afro-Dominican religious procession of music and dance performed during Semana Santa (Holy Week) in the sugar bateyes, especially the east/southeast (San Pedro de Macoris, La Romana) and border provinces. It blends Vodu Dominicano (Las 21 Divisiones), folk Catholicism and African elements. Bands parade led by a 'dueno,' with male dancers fronting, then female dancers, then musicians; processions stop at crossroads for rituals. Instruments include futubas/vaksin (bamboo trumpets), improvised tin trumpets, palos (drums), guiras, maracas, whistles and whips (Smithsonian Folkways; Univ. of Maryland dissertation).
card.insight: Ethnomusicologist June Rosenberg characterized Gaga as distinctively Dominican rather than Haitian even though it derives from Haitian Rara, reflecting how the batey context produced an independent Creole identity (Univ. of Maryland dissertation, Hernandez-Sang).
card.image_significance: Haitian-rooted Lenten processional. A representative image shows ceremonial regalia in a ritual context — imagery should be handled respectfully, not as spectacle — batey, Dominican Republic.
